title: EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook (February 2027) — the first revision of the newly-rolled 2028 forecast line
source: EST: eia.gov/outlooks/steo/release_schedule.php, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 54,906 bytes) by the eia-steo-2027-01-12 never-assessed initial research and read from the RAW HTML table, whose 2027 row is "February 2027 | 02/09/2027" with a blank Notes cell; the same page states the release window as 12:00-12:15 pm ET. Reproduces independently from the page's own rule ("the first Tuesday following the first Thursday of each month", a Federal holiday on the preceding Monday pushing to Wednesday): 2027-02-04 is a Thursday, the following Tuesday is 02-09, and 2027-02-08 is not a Federal holiday. Filed estimate on the standing EIA grounds — this calendar defines no `confirmed` prefix for the EIA, and a discovering lane never self-confirms an event it found in-sweep — not on date doubt
notes: Discovered during eia-steo-2027-01-12's never-assessed initial research (2026-09-09), off the same raw EIA release-schedule table that dates the January edition. Proposed for one reason beyond calendar completeness, and it is the direct consequence of that session's verified finding. The January edition is the HORIZON-ROLL edition: EIA's own archives show the indicator table's columns moving 2024|2025|2026 in archives/nov25.pdf to 2025|2026|2027 in archives/jan26.pdf, so 2027-01-12 publishes the first 2028 forecast lines and 2027-02-09 is the FIRST REVISION of them. A brand-new out-year printed once is a forecast; the same line revised a month later is the first evidence of which direction EIA is being pushed - which is what makes 01-12 -> 02-09 a genuine two-document read for the national 2028 electricity-consumption line that ai-energy-constraint.md's demand leg has never had an out-year for. The measured hint that motivates the pair is thin and is labelled thin: on the only two January editions inside the 2-year Yahoo window (2025-01-14, 2026-01-13) crude ran ABOVE its pooled STEO-day base rate (CL=F 2.22% vs 1.34%, BZ=F 1.93% vs 1.35%, XLE 1.25% vs 0.94%) while equities went quieter than an ordinary STEO day - the signature a horizon roll would produce if it produced one at all. n=2, no significance test, two different macro regimes; it is registered as a forward test on the January edition rather than asserted, and this proposal exists partly so the February revision can adjudicate it. Filed `low` on the sibling entries' reasoning: a forecast publication sets no policy and moves no equity tape. Secondary note for the owning lane: 2027-02-09 sits AFTER the January 26-27 FOMC (FED: fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09 - no SEP asterisk on that meeting), so unlike eia-steo-2026-12-08 it carries no blackout or pre-decision-freeze complication.
